title: Lavender solid perfume
subtitle: A pocket-size beeswax balm scented with lavender and a trace of vanilla
excerpt: A solid perfume made with beeswax, jojoba, and lavender essential oil with a small amount of vanilla absolute for warmth. Scooped with a fingertip and applied to pulse points. Melts on contact with skin warmth. Fills one small 10 g tin. Shelf life 12 months.
sourceNotes: Solid perfume formulation: beeswax 30-35% + carrier oil 55-60% + fragrance 10-15% by weight. A higher beeswax percentage gives a firmer, lipstick-like texture; lower gives a soft balm. 30% beeswax here produces a spreadable but non-greasy solid in a small tin. Jojoba as carrier: very stable, absorbs quickly, non-greasy. Lavender EO (Lavandula angustifolia): major constituents linalool + linalyl acetate; good IFRA leave-on compliance. Vanilla absolute (5-fold or CO2 extract): provides a warm base note; very small amount is sufficient. Total fragrance load 15% is the upper limit for a solid anhydrous product applied to the wrist.

recipe.batchNotes: Make 4 tins at once (40 g batch), they make good gifts and the beeswax scales cleanly.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ready once set (60 minutes). Keeps 12 months.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 12 months. Anhydrous; no preservative needed. Jojoba is very stable. Discard if the balm develops a musty smell.

glossaryTerms.definition: Areas of the skin where blood vessels lie close to the surface, wrists, inner elbows, behind the knees, base of the throat. Body heat at these points warms the perfume, releasing the scent.
A preparation containing no water phase. Anhydrous solid perfumes are shelf-stable without a preservative because there is no moisture for micro-organisms to grow in.

content.text: Melt the beeswax and jojoba in a heatproof vessel over simmering water until the wax is fully melted.
Remove from heat. Cool to 40°C, then stir in the lavender essential oil and vanilla absolute.
Pour into the tin. Leave undisturbed for 60 minutes until set.
12 months at room temperature. Keep out of direct sunlight and away from heat, which will soften the balm. The lavender note is most vivid in the first 6 months.
